World 1900-1964: historical reconstruction by Pinto et al. (2023) as redistributed by OWID; bands are analyst-assumed (approx. 5th-95th percentile), not published. Biomass and waste; peat is treated separately where IRENA gives it (elec_gen_peat).

Modelled: OWID "other renewables" (Pinto et al. 2023 / EI; geothermal plus negligible tidal) scaled by the 1980-1990 mean ratio of EIA geothermal to other renewables (0.947). Low = 0.85x, high = 1.0x of other renewables (assumed).
IRENA electricity statistics 2026 H2 "Peat and peat products" generation, sum of countries; bands assumed +-10%. Peat is not in OWID bioenergy.

OWID series (Energy Institute from 1965; Etemad and Luciani 1991 for 1900-1979; Smil 2017 for world 1800-1899; NIC/Fouquet for UK before 1900). Energy units as published. Bands assumed (approx. 5th-95th percentile): +-20% before 1900, +-10% to 1964, +-5% to 1984, +-3% from 1985 (x1.5 for countries).

Modelled: energy (TWh) divided by a calorific divisor c(y) MWh/t, c=6.85 (UK calibration, S0230/S0231) up to 1900, falling linearly to the 1985-1989 mean ratio of OWID energy to EIA tonnes (6.53 MWh/t) in 1985 (rising lignite and sub-bituminous share). Low tonnes use 8.14 MWh/t before 1985 scaled likewise (1.19 x c); high tonnes use 0.85 x c. 6.85 and 8.14 MWh/t are the extremes found by the coal survey.

Thermal energy of coal burned for electricity = coal generation / efficiency. Efficiency proxy (assumed bounds +-15%): UK coal generation / UK power-station coal use at 6.85 MWh/t (S0231, 1920-1964), mean of UK and US (S0232 plus EIA MER Tables 2.6 and 7.2a, S0804) 1949-1964, US alone from 1965; 0.07 (0.05-0.10) before 1920. Real world fleet efficiency may differ (older Soviet/Chinese plant lower).

Share of world coal energy consumed in power generation = coal_burn_power_twh / coal consumption (TWh). Products and quotients bounded in log-space quadrature (METHODS 11.1). Check anchors: UK 2.5% (1913), 8.4% (1938), 15% (1949); US 18.6% (1950), 91% (2000).

Total ash from coal burned for power = thermal coal burn (TWh) / calorific divisor c(y) (t) x ash yield. Ash yield central 0.12 (low 0.08, high 0.16; coal survey range 0.10-0.16 for ash content, S0230 notes and availability.csv; assumption). World coal anchors for validation: 280 Mt ash (1985), about 780 Mt coal combustion products (2010) in the Task 1.3 survey.

Fly-ash fraction of power-station ash: 0.30 to 1920 rising linearly to 0.80 by 1960 and constant after (assumed: stoker/grate firing dominant early, pulverised-coal with collectors later; coal survey notes stokers 15% fly). Modelled net capacity addition = change in 3-year-smoothed world generation (OWID/EI/Pinto) / (8.766 x CF), CF = IRENA world fleet-average realised coal capacity factor 2000-2005 (0.85) held constant. Retirements and CF drift are ignored; bands -50%/+60% assumed. Negative changes set to zero.

Modelled net capacity addition = change in 3-year-smoothed world generation (OWID/EI/Pinto) / (8.766 x CF), CF = IRENA world fleet-average realised gas capacity factor 2000-2005 (0.59) held constant. Retirements and CF drift are ignored; bands -50%/+60% assumed. Negative changes set to zero.

Net MW(e) of reactors with first grid connection in year y, IAEA RDS-2 No. 45 Tables 14-16 (units that connected and closed are included; reconnections after long shutdown are not counted). Bands +-3% assumed.

Fraunhofer ISE Photovoltaics Report (14 July 2026): thin film 16 GWp of 706 GWp module production in 2025 (First Solar only; CdTe), c-Si 98%. Only this anchor was extractable (other years are chart-only); CdTe/CIGS split not given. Bands assumed.

World fleet-average realised capacity factor = IRENA generation / (year-end installed capacity x 8.766 TWh per GW-year); year-end capacity overstates average capacity in fast-growing fleets (wind, PV), so growth-years are biased low (bands +-8% assumed, wider for wind/PV in notes).

World nuclear generation (OWID/Ember/EI) / (mean-of-year connected capacity from RDS-2 reconstruction x 8.766); capacity includes units in suspended operation, so CF is biased low when many units are suspended (Japan 2011-2020). Bands +-10% assumed.

Single vintage (technology as of about 2010). Bands +-20%/+25% assumed (AR5 gives a point value).

IPCC AR5 WGIII Annex III Table A.III.1 full-load hours range (min/max) divided by 8,766 h; central = midpoint of the AR5 range (the table gives only min and max). Planning ranges are wide: use cf_realised_* for vintage trends.
